title: Toad in the Hole
subtitle: Sausages baked in crisp Yorkshire pudding batter
excerpt: The great British batter dish: fat pork sausages rested in a ripping-hot tin of dripping then submerged in Yorkshire pudding batter that rises dramatically around them in the oven, crisp at the edges and yielding in the centre. Serve with onion gravy.

recipe.sourceNotes: Toad in the hole is a British dish first documented in the eighteenth century, where it referred to meat (often leftovers, not sausages) baked in batter. The modern version with pork sausages became standard in the nineteenth century. The name's origin is disputed but the most plausible explanation is simply the visual: the sausages peering out of the risen batter resemble toads emerging from holes in the ground. The batter is identical to Yorkshire pudding batter and the same principles apply: the fat must be smoking hot before the batter goes in; the batter must be rested; the oven must not be opened during baking or the pudding will collapse. Good sausages, browned before the batter is added, are the other essential.

content.text: The fat must be smoking hot. Cold fat poured over with batter produces a flat, greasy result. Brown the sausages in the tin first so they are already partially cooked; raw sausages in the batter can release steam and prevent proper rising. Do not open the oven while the batter is rising.

Make the batter: whisk the flour, salt, eggs, and half the milk to a smooth paste. Whisk in the remaining milk until the batter is the consistency of double cream. Add the mustard if using. Leave to rest for at least 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 220°C / fan 200°C / gas 7. Pour the oil into a large, shallow roasting tin (about 30 x 25 cm) and heat in the oven for 5 minutes. Add the sausages and cook in the hot oil for 15 minutes, turning once, until browned. The oil should be smoking.

Working quickly, pour the batter around the sausages in one motion, filling the tin. Immediately return to the oven. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes without opening the oven until the batter is risen, golden, and very crisp at the edges. Serve immediately with onion gravy.
